title: SPECIAL ACT ON RELIEF AND SUPPORT FOR VICTIMS OF THE DECEMBER 29 PASSENGER AIRCRAFT DISASTER
title_original: 12ㆍ29여객기참사 피해구제 및 지원 등을 위한 특별법
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to commemorate the persons who lost their lives in the passenger aircraft disaster that occurred at Muan International Airport on December 29, 2024, and to support the recovery of the victims' daily lives and their communities by providing prompt relief for damage suffered by the victims, as well as assistance for their livelihoods and psychological stability.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. The term "December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster" means the incident in which a passenger aircraft operating as Jeju Air Flight 2216 was involved in an accident at Muan International Airport, Mangun-myeon, Muan-gun, Jeollanam-do, on December 29, 2024, resulting in a large number of persons who lost their lives and victims;
  2. The term "person who lost their life" means a person who died among those who were on board the relevant passenger aircraft at the time of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster;
  3. The term "victim" means any of the following persons:
  a. A person, other than a person who lost their life, who was on board the relevant passenger aircraft at the time of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster;
  b. The spouse (including a de facto spouse; hereinafter the same shall apply), lineal ascendants or descendants, or siblings of a person who lost their life (hereafter in this Article referred to as "bereaved family members");
  c. The spouse, lineal ascendants or descendants, or siblings of a person falling under item a.
  4. The term "affected areas" means Gwangju Metropolitan City and Jeollanam-do, where a large number of persons who lost their lives and victims occurred as a result of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster;
  5. The term "bereaved family organization" means an organization composed of bereaved family members, as prescribed by presidential decree.

Article 3 (Rights of victims) Victims shall have the following rights throughout all processes, including the investigation of the truth of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster, damage relief, and support:
  1. The right to be informed and to be heard;
  2. The right to be protected from hatred and receive necessary assistance without discrimination;
  3. The right to protection of personal information and privacy;
  4. The right to remember, commemorate, and mourn, and to be remembered, commemorated, and mourned;
  5. The right to receive necessary support, including livelihood support, medical support, psychological treatment, caregiving support, and legal support;
  6. The right to participate in follow-up projects, including commemorative projects and community recovery projects, by expressing opinions and otherwise engaging in such projects;
  7. The right to receive compensation and damages;
  8. Other rights of victims recognized under the Constitution of the Republic of Korea and international human rights treaties.

Article 4 (Responsibilities of the State and local governments) (1) The State and local governments (hereinafter referred to as the "State, etc.") shall formulate and implement comprehensive policy measures to support victims and affected areas and to prevent the recurrence of similar accidents, including the establishment of facilities and equipment and the expansion of personnel.
  (2) The State, etc. shall actively cooperate in performing duties to guarantee the rights of victims, including damage relief and support provided under this Act.
  (3) The State shall take budgetary measures necessary to support victims and affected areas and to prevent the recurrence of similar accidents.

Article 5 (Prevention of secondary victimization) (1) The State, etc. shall formulate and implement measures to prevent acts that publicly damage the reputation or insult the dignity of persons who lost their lives or victims by any of the following means (hereinafter referred to as "secondary victimization"), and shall take proactive measures, including legal and administrative support:
  1. The use of newspapers, magazines, broadcasting, other publications, or information and communications networks defined in Article 2 (1) 1 of the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection;
  2. Displaying, posting, or screening of exhibits or performances;
  3. Statements made at other publicly conducted discussions, briefings, press conferences, assemblies, street speeches, and similar events.
  (2) The State, etc. shall cooperate with the media, educational institutions, and other entities to raise awareness of the need to protect victims arising from the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster and to conduct public relations and educational activities for the prevention of secondary victimization.

Article 6 (Relationship to other statutes) This Act shall take precedence over other statutes with respect to matters regarding damage relief and support related to the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster.

CHAPTER II SUPPORT FOR VICTIMS

Article 7 (Principles of support) (1) The State, etc. shall devise support measures for the recovery of victims from physical, psychological, and economic harm.
  (2) The State, etc. shall comprehensively support victims across all aspects of daily life, including education, health, welfare, caregiving, and employment, including living expenses, so that victims may secure the living conditions they need.
  (3) The State, etc. shall provide victims, including foreign nationals, persons with disabilities, and children, with necessary technical, administrative, and financial support.

Article 8 (Guarantee of participation of victims) In formulating and implementing plans to support victims and affected areas, the State, etc. shall hear the opinions of victims and other relevant persons and reflect such opinions to the greatest extent possible.

Article 9 (Support for economic revitalization and community recovery) (1) The State shall implement special support measures reflecting the opinions from affected areas in order to promote economic revitalization, including culture and tourism, and to support community recovery in affected areas.
  (2) The special support measures under paragraph (1) may include financial support for persons who have suffered damage as a result of restrictions on business activities and other consequences arising from the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster.

Article 10 (Living assistance benefits) (1) The State may provide a victim with the following benefits (hereinafter referred to as "living assistance benefits, etc."):
  1. Living assistance benefit: expenses necessary to assist the victim in maintaining their livelihood;
  2. Medical support allowance: expenses incurred for the treatment, nursing care, or use of assistive devices for physical or mental illnesses or injuries, and any sequelae thereof, arising from the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster.
  (2) With respect to living assistance benefits, etc., the main clause of Article 3 (2) of the National Basic Living Security Act shall not apply for a period determined by the Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25, within a limit of 1 year.
  (3) Matters necessary for the scope of payment of living assistance benefits, etc., the calculation of amounts, methods of payment, periods of payment, and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Special support allowances for persons who lost their life under 15 years of age) (1) The State may provide special support allowances with respect to a person who lost their life under 15 years of age.
  (2) The amount of the special support allowances under paragraph (1) shall be determined in consideration of the level of insurance proceeds or mutual aid benefits payable under insurance or mutual aid schemes in which a local government has enrolled its residents as insured persons under its ordinance.
  (3) Matters necessary for the standards, procedures, and other details for the payment of the special support allowances under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Support for psychological counseling) (1) The State, etc. shall provide necessary support, such as psychological counseling and daily life counseling, for the psychological stability and social adaptation of victims (including the spouses of the lineal ascendants or descendants of a person who lost their life, and the spouses of siblings thereof; hereafter in Article 13 the same shall apply) and persons who participated in rescue, recovery, medical treatment, handling of remains, investigation, volunteer activities, or news coverage, etc.
  (2) Matters necessary for the details and methods of the support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13 (Support for examinations and treatment of psychological symptoms and mental illness) (1) The State, etc. shall provide support to ensure that a victim may undergo medical examinations or treatment for psychological symptoms and mental illness, etc. that have been aggravated as a result of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster.
  (2) Matters necessary for the details and methods of the support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Recovery leave for employees) (1) Where an employee who qualifies as a victim under this Act applies, within 1 year from the enforcement of this Act, for a leave of absence in order to recover from physical or mental damage arising from the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster, the employer shall permit such leave (hereinafter referred to as "recovery leave"); provided, where there is a physician's written opinion, or in other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, an application for recovery leave may be made within 3 years from the enforcement of this Act.
  (2) The period of recovery leave shall not exceed 6 months; provided, where there is a physician's written opinion, or in other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such period may be extended by up to 6 months.
  (3) An employer shall not dismiss an employee or otherwise subject the employee to unfavorable treatment on the grounds of recovery leave, and shall not dismiss the employee during the period of recovery leave; provided, this shall not apply where the employer is unable to continue the business.
  (4) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for applying for recovery leave shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Support for recovery leave for employees) (1) Where an employer grants recovery leave to an employee, the State shall pay all or part of the employment retention costs incurred by the employer with respect to that employee.
  (2) Matters necessary for the details of payment of employment retention costs under paragraph (1), as well as for the application and payment procedures therefor, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Support for education expenses) If a victim falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the State, etc. may support admission fees, tuition fees, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
  1. An infant or young child who attends a daycare center under any subparagraph of Article 10 of the Child Care Act, or a young child who attends a kindergarten under any subparagraph of Article 7 of the Early Childhood Education Act;
  2. A student who has been confirmed for admission to or is enrolled in a school under the subparagraphs of Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
  3. A student who has been confirmed for admission to or is enrolled in a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act.

Article 17 (Special cases concerning the Emergency Aid and Support Act and the Child Care Support Act) (1) Among victims under this Act, those prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be deemed persons in need of emergency aid under Article 5 of the Emergency Welfare Support Act.
  (2) Where a victim experiences a gap in childcare for their child as a result of activities related to recovery from the damage, the victim may be given priority access to childcare services defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Child Care Support Act.
  (3) With respect to a minor victim whose holder of parental authority lost their life as a result of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster, the State, etc. shall establish measures for protection and support applicable until the minor reaches the age of majority.
  (4) Matters necessary for the standards, periods, methods, and procedures for the support, etc. under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Support for daily living care) The State, etc. shall provide support for the following care services necessary for a victim's recovery and return to daily life:
  1. Assistance with household activities to maintain daily living;
  2. Meal support services to improve health and nutritional status;
  3. Other services necessary to support the victim's recovery of daily life.

Article 19 (Support for legal counseling) (1) The State may provide support, including legal counseling and representation in litigation, to victims.
  (2) Expenses incurred for support under paragraph (1) may be borne by the State, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Matters necessary for the requirements, details, and procedures of support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Request for cooperation to alleviate financial burden of victims) The State, etc. may request necessary cooperation from relevant public institutions, financial institutions, and other relevant agencies or organizations in order to alleviate the financial burdens of victims who are experiencing economic hardship due to financial debts.

Article 21 (Development and implementation of community recovery programs) (1) The State, etc. shall develop and implement programs to promote the psychological stability of victims and residents of affected areas and the recovery of the community, taking into consideration the following matters:
  1. The characteristics of victims and residents of the affected areas, such as nationality, race, religion, gender, age, and occupation;
  2. The prevention of victims and affected residents from leaving their communities and the improvement of their quality of life;
  3. The promotion of the distinctive culture of affected areas and the strengthening of community ties;
  4. Participation by, and collaboration with, relevant nonprofit private organizations, public-interest organizations, clubs, and other related entities located in the affected areas in the fields of health, welfare, education, culture, sports, etc.
  (2) Where a victim participates in a program under paragraph (1), the State, etc. may provide subsidies to cover all or part of the expenses incurred in such participation. In such cases, matters necessary for the details, methods, and periods of such support shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The State, etc. shall fully collect the opinions of the victims and the residents of the affected areas when developing the program under paragraph (1).
  (4) The State, etc. may conduct examination, research, etc. necessary for the development and implementation of the programs under paragraph (1).

Article 22 (Establishment of integrated community facilities) (1) Where necessary for the recovery of the community, relevant local governments may, in consultation with the State and bereaved family organizations, establish and operate integrated community facilities that provide psychological counseling and services in the areas of health, welfare, care, education, labor, culture, etc.
  (2) In order to effectively support community recovery, the head of an integrated community facility shall, where necessary, have the facility's staff visit the homes of victims, etc. to provide the psychological counseling and services in the areas of health, welfare, care, education, labor, and culture under paragraph (1).
  (3) Where a relevant local government establishes and operates integrated community facilities under paragraph (1), the State may provide subsidies to cover part of the expenses necessary therefor.
  (4) Matters necessary for the establishment and operation of integrated community facilities under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government.

Article 23 (Operation of the advisory group) (1) The Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25 may operate an advisory group for the support of victims and the protection of their rights (hereinafter referred to as the "Advisory Group").
  (2) The Advisory Group shall be composed of up to 20 advisory members, who shall be commissioned by the chairperson of the Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25 after hearing the opinions of bereaved family organizations.
  (3) The State may pay allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses to advisory members within the budget.
  (4) Other matters necessary for the organization and operation of the Advisory Group shall be prescribed by the rules of the Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25.

CHAPTER III COMMEMORATIVE PROJECTS

Article 24 (Implementation of commemorative projects and long-term follow-up studies) (1) For the purpose of commemorating persons who lost their lives and providing education for the prevention of aviation safety accidents, the State, etc. may implement the following projects; provided, if a local government implements such projects, the State, etc. may provide support therefor:
  1. Development of memorial parks;
  2. Construction of memorial halls;
  3. Collection, preservation, management, and exhibition of materials of memorial halls, and research and studies thereon;
  4. Public relations and education regarding materials of memorial halls and commemorative projects, and the production and distribution of various publications related thereto;
  5. Construction of memorial monuments;
  6. Installation and operation of training facilities for the prevention of aviation safety accidents;
  7. Other related projects.
  (2) For the purpose of preventing social isolation of victims, managing sequelae, strengthening disaster response systems, and developing effective support policies, the State, etc. shall conduct long-term follow-up studies on the physical and mental health conditions of victims, etc.
  (3) A memorial hall under paragraph (1) shall be equipped with facilities and equipment, and staffed with professional personnel necessary for their operation, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to ensure systematic management, safe preservation, and efficient utilization of records.
  (4) Matters necessary for the requirements, details, and procedures for the implementation of commemorative projects under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 25 (December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster Victim Support and Commemoration Committee) (1) To deliberate on important matters regarding support for victims and commemorative projects for persons who lost their lives under this Act, the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster Victim Support and Commemoration Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Support and Commemoration Committee") shall be established under the jurisdiction of the Prime Minister.
  (2) The Support and Commemoration Committee shall deliberate and resolve on the following matters:
  1. Matters regarding support for victims, including identification of victims, provision of living assistance benefits, psychological counseling, recovery leave, educational expenses, and support for community recovery;
  2. Matters regarding commemorative projects, including the creation of memorial parks and the construction of memorial halls and monuments;
  3. Matters regarding the designation of a foundation or association under Article 30;
  4. Other matters related to support for victims and commemorative projects that the chairperson of the Support and Commemoration Committee deems necessary.
  (3) The Support and Commemoration Committee shall be composed of up to 20 members, including 2 chairpersons.
  (4) One chairperson of the Support and Commemoration Committee shall be the Prime Minister, and the other chairperson shall be designated by the President from among the civilian members.
  (5) Members of the Support and Commemoration Committee shall be appointed or commissioned by the chairperson, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, from among relevant public officials, persons with extensive knowledge and experience recommended by bereaved family organizations, and members of bereaved families.
  (6) A member who is a member of a bereaved family shall be disqualified from the deliberation and resolution of matters regarding support for victims.
  (7) For the purpose of allocating and performing part of its duties, the Support and Commemoration Committee shall establish a Victim Support Sectoral Committee and a Sectoral Committee for Commemorative Projects for Persons Who Lost Their Lives.
  (8) The chairperson of each Sectoral Committee and the members thereof under paragraph (7) shall be designated by the chairperson from among the members of the Support and Commemoration Committee; provided, a member who is a bereaved family member shall not serve as a member of the Victim Support Sectoral Committee.
  (9) The composition and operation of the Support and Commemoration Committee and each Sectoral Committee, procedures for the appointment of members, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Support Task Force for Victims of December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster) (1) In order to efficiently promote projects to support victims and affected areas under this Act, collect and review relevant materials necessary for the deliberation and resolution by the Support and Commemoration Committee, promote commemorative projects, and otherwise support the administrative affairs and operation of the Support and Commemoration Committee, the Support Task Force for the Victims of the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster (hereinafter referred to as "Task Force") shall be established in the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
  (2) When necessary for the performance of the Task Force's duties, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, and relevant agencies and organizations to dispatch affiliated public officials or executives and employees.
  (3) Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Task Force shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 27 (Establishment and operation of information system) (1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may establish and operate an information system to efficiently perform support projects for victims and affected areas under this Act.
  (2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may request relevant agencies to provide data where necessary for the operation of the information system. In such cases, the relevant agencies in receipt of such request shall comply therewith unless there is good cause.
  (3) Other matters necessary for the establishment and operation of the information system shall be determined by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 28 (Names of commemorative facilities) The Support and Commemoration Committee shall collect public opinion, through public solicitation or other means, on the names of memorial parks, memorial halls, and memorial monuments (hereinafter referred to as "commemorative facilities"), and, in consultation with bereaved family organizations, deliberate on and decide such names.

Article 29 (Special cases concerning installation of commemorative facilities) (1) The State, etc. may establish commemorative facilities, notwithstanding relevant statutes such as the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, the School Health Act, and the Act on Special Measures for Designation and Management of Development Restriction Zones.
  (2) Matters necessary for the installation of commemorative facilities under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 30 (Support for foundations or associations) (1) The State may make contributions or pay subsidy to a foundation established to commemorate persons who lost their lives and to contribute to the prevention of recurrence of aviation safety accidents, etc. by performing the following projects (referring to a non-profit corporation established under Article 32 of the Civil Act and selected by the Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25 (2) 3), for a period of 10 years after its establishment:
  1. Operation and management of commemorative facilities and the performance of memorial services;
  2. Projects regarding the prevention of safety accidents and the promotion of a safety culture;
  3. Support projects for the psychological stability, livelihood stabilization, and social reintegration of victims;
  4. Other projects necessary to achieve the purposes for which the foundation is established.
  (2) A public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions may provide subsidies to cover expenses necessary for the operation of an association (referring to a non-profit corporation established under Article 32 of the Civil Act that has been selected by the Support and Commemoration Committee under Article 25 (2) 3) which is composed of bereaved family members and established for the purpose of contributing to the commemoration of persons who lost their lives, the self-help activities of bereaved families, and the prevention of the recurrence of aviation safety accidents, until the establishment of the foundation under paragraph (1), within a period not exceeding 10 years from the date this Act enters into force.
  (3) The State, etc. may entrust commemorative projects, such as the operation and management of commemorative facilities, to the foundation under paragraph (1).
  (4) Matters necessary for the support under paragraph (2), including the supporting entity, criteria, details, and period of support, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Special cases concerning acceptance of donated money and goods) (1) The foundation and association under Article 30 may receive any voluntarily entrusted donations to the extent meeting its business objectives, notwithstanding the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 5 (2) of the Act on Collection and Use of Donations and Promotion of Donation Culture.
  (2) Matters necessary for the procedures for accepting donated money and goods under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 32 (Reporting on status of accident investigation and victim support) (1) In order to ascertain the status of accident investigations and the status of victim support relating to the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster, the Support and Commemoration Committee and bereaved family organizations may request relevant central administrative agencies, relevant local governments, and other relevant administrative agencies or organizations (hereinafter referred to as "relevant agencies, etc.") to submit reports and relevant materials as necessary. In such cases, the relevant agencies, etc. requested to submit reports or materials shall comply therewith unless there is good cause not to do so.
  (2) The Support and Commemoration Committee and bereaved family organizations may present their opinions regarding the status of the accident investigation and the status of victim support.

CHAPTER IV SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 33 (Duty of confidentiality) No person who is or was a member or staff member of the Support and Commemoration Committee and the Support Group (hereinafter referred to as the "Support and Commemoration Committee, etc.") or who is or was an advisory member of the Advisory Group shall provide or disclose to any other person any information, documents, materials, or objects that constitute confidential information, or shall use such information for purposes other than the performance of their duties.

Article 34 (Prohibition on impersonation of qualifications) (1) No person shall impersonate a member or staff member of the Support and Commemoration Committee, etc., or an advisory member of the Advisory Group, and exercise the authority of the Support and Commemoration Committee, etc., or the Advisory Group.
  (2) No person shall, under the pretext of supporting victims, organize a for-profit organization or engage in collective or individual activities for profit-making purposes.

Article 35 (Protection of rights) Rights arising under this Act shall not be transferred, seized, or provided as collateral.

Article 36 (Recovery of unjust enrichment) (1) Where a person who has received monetary payments, such as living assistance benefits, or other forms of support under this Act falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the State, etc. shall recover an amount equivalent thereto:
  1. Where such payment or support was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where such payment or support was made by mistake or error.
  (2) Where recovery is made under paragraph (1), if the person obligated to make restitution fails to return the amount within a specified period, it may be collected in accordance with the examples of compulsory collection of national taxes or disposition on delinquent local taxes.

Article 37 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) Members of the Support and Commemoration Committee who are not public officials shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

CHAPTER V PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 38 (Penalty provisions) (1) A person who, by fraud or other improper means, receives or causes another person to receive living assistance benefits, etc. under Article 10 or special support allowances under Article 11 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 5 years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won.
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won:
  1. A person who provides or discloses to another person, or uses for purposes other than the performance of duties, any information, documents, materials, or objects that constitute confidential information, in violation of Article 33;
  2. A person who impersonates a member or staff member of the Support and Commemoration Committee, etc., or an advisory member of the Advisory Group, and exercises the authority of the Support and Commemoration Committee, etc., or the Advisory Group, in violation of Article 34 (1);
  3. A person who organizes an organization or engages in collective or individual activities, in violation of Article 34 (2).

Article 39 (Attempt) A person who attempts to commit the offense under Article 38 (1) shall be punished.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20954, Apr. 29, 2025>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force two months after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Preparatory acts for enforcement of this Act)
The appointment or commissioning of members and staff members of the Support and Commemoration Committee, etc., the commissioning of advisory members of the Advisory Group, the enactment and promulgation of the rules of the Support and Commemoration Committee regarding the enforcement of this Act, and the organization of bereaved family organizations may be made prior to the enforcement of this Act.
Article 3 (Special cases concerning overlapping support)
Various forms of support under this Act may be provided to victims who, as of the date this Act enters into force, have received or are receiving support of the same nature due to the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster, excluding the overlapping portions thereof.
Article 4 (Special cases concerning examinations and treatment of psychological symptoms and mental illness)
Article 13 shall also apply to examinations or treatment received, from December 29, 2024 to the date this Act enters into force, by victims (including spouses of lineal descendants and ascendants of persons who lost their lives, and spouses of siblings) for psychological symptoms and mental illness, etc. that were aggravated due to the December 29 Passenger Aircraft Disaster.
Article 5 (Special cases concerning application of recovery leave)
Any period during which the Minister of Employment and Labor provided support to an employer for special suspension of business or leave of absence under Article 14 (1) prior to the enforcement of this Act shall be included in the period of recovery leave under Article 14 (2).
Article 6 (Special cases concerning support for employees' recovery leave)
Article 15 shall also apply where an employer allowed recovery leave during the period from December 29, 2024 to the date this Act enters into force.
